chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Faddal, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abd al-A'la ibn A'yan who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'I was born from the lineage of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and I know the Book of God; in it is the beginning of creation and what shall come to pass until the Day of Resurrection, and in it is the news of the heavens and the news of the earth and the news of Paradise and the news of the Fire and the news of what has been and the news of what shall come to pass. I know all that just as I look upon my own palm.
Indeed God says: in it is a clear exposition of every thing. [16:89]

key_terms.بَدْءُ الْخَلْقِ: The beginning of creation — the Quran's account of cosmological origins
key_terms.تِبْيَانُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ: A clear exposition of every thing — Quranic phrase (16:89) affirming the Quran's all-encompassing nature
key_terms.كَفِّي: My palm — a vivid metaphor for absolute clarity and immediacy of knowledge
key_terms.كِتَابُ اللَّهِ: The Book of God — the Quran, the comprehensive divine revelation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about his knowledge of the Quran and its comprehensive contents?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) asserting his comprehensive knowledge of the Quran — knowledge that encompasses the beginning of creation, future events until the Day of Judgment, and the realities of heaven and hell. He illustrates the clarity and immediacy of this knowledge by comparing it to looking at his own hand. He closes by citing Quran 16:89, which states that the Quran contains a clear exposition of everything, implying that the Imam's knowledge of the Quran gives him knowledge of all things. This teaching was directed at his close companions to affirm the doctrinal position that the Imam possesses comprehensive knowledge of divine revelation.
